claim_scope: finite planning horizon can change the first action in a fixed delayed-reward MDP
a terminal value can extend a one-step planner in the same fixture
replanning after an observed disturbance can outperform executing the stale suffix
expected return, empirical lower-tail return, and a fixed chance constraint can rank the same hand-authored actions differently

data.name: procedural delayed-reward MDP and observation labels

limitations: known deterministic rules rather than a learned world model
exhaustive enumeration rather than CEM, MCTS, or continuous optimization
value-equivalence check covers one value function and does not establish universal equivalence
five equally weighted hand-authored outcomes do not estimate real tail probabilities or safety
no simulator, neural network, policy learning, GPU, robot, or vehicle
